examples.claim: KV cache of a single LLaMA-13B sequence takes up to 1.7GB
examples.source: Blog: 'Large: Takes up to 1.7GB for a single sequence in LLaMA-13B.'

examples.claim: Query 'forth' multiplied with block 0 keys 'Four score and seven', then with V_j into o_i
examples.source: Paper §4.1 Fig. 5 walk-through (blocks 'Four score and seven', 'years ago our fathers', 'brought forth').

examples.claim: Block engine allocates contiguous GPU DRAM split into physical blocks; block table entry holds physical block number and #filled
examples.source: Paper §4.2: 'a block engine allocates a contiguous chunk of GPU DRAM ... Each block table entry records the corresponding physical blocks of a logical block and the number of filled positions.'

examples.claim: Parallel sampling with A1, A2: logical blocks 0,1 map to physical 7,1, both with reference count 2
examples.source: Paper §4.4: 'the reference counts for physical blocks 7 and 1 are both 2.'

examples.claim: Beam search k=4: block 0 shared by all, candidate 3 diverges at block 2, candidates 0-2 share three blocks; freed set {2,4,5,8}
examples.source: Paper §4.4 Fig. 9 text: 'Candidate 3 digresses from others from the second block. Candidates 0-2 share the first 3 blocks ... (blocks 2, 4, 5, 8)'.

examples.claim: Memory sharing cuts parallel-sampling and beam-search memory by up to 55% and raises throughput up to 2.2x
examples.source: Blog: 'cutting their memory usage by up to 55%. This can translate into up to 2.2x improvement in throughput.' (v15's mis-tie to the 3-output benchmark is gone)

examples.claim: V1 prefix caching costs <1% throughput at 0% hit rate, so it is on by default in V1; off in V0; v0.8.5.post1 default V0 off / V1 on
examples.source: V1 blog: 'less than 1% decrease in throughput even when the cache hit rate is 0% ... we now enable prefix caching by default in V1'; v0.8.5.post1 engine args: 'Disabled by default for V0. Enabled by default for V1.' (now correctly called the V1 blog, fixing v15's 'third-party' misattribution)

examples.claim: Swapped-out blocks never exceed GPU physical blocks, so CPU swap space is bounded by the GPU KV-cache allocation
examples.source: Paper §4.5: 'the number of blocks swapped to the CPU RAM never exceeds the number of total physical blocks in the GPU RAM'.

examples.claim: 512-token budget: A 1 + B 1 + C 510; 1,200-token prompt chunked 510 + 510 + 180
examples.source: Writer's labelled example ('가상으로'); arithmetic holds (512 = 1+1+510; 1,200 = 510+510+180); dict shape from V1 blog '{request_id: num_tokens}'.

examples.claim: Compiled CUDA kernels are binary-incompatible with other CUDA/PyTorch versions even with the same PyTorch version under other build settings; conda PyTorch statically links NCCL
examples.source: gpu.cuda.inc.md set-up-using-python note and paragraph, verbatim in meaning.

examples.claim: Assumed 24GB x 0.9 = 21.6GB, minus ~3GB BF16 weights = 18.6GB; 2 x 28 x 2 x 128 x 2 = 28,672 bytes per token
examples.source: Labelled assumptions; arithmetic exact; 28 layers / 2 KV heads / head dim 128 match Qwen2.5-1.5B's config (1536 hidden / 12 heads); formula from Fastio.

examples.claim: Run:ai, A100 40GB, Llama-2-7b, 64 QPS: throughput peaks at max-num-seqs 192, where preemptions first appear; larger batches add preemptions and lose throughput
examples.source: Run:ai Exp. 2: 'send 64 queries per second. Preemptions start occuring at a batch size of 192 ... coinciding with the throughput peak'; Table 4 at 64 QPS peaks at 192 (2,852).

examples.claim: quantization accepts 'awq', 'gptq', 'fp8' (experimental); Unsloth says fp8 KV cache cuts memory 50%
examples.source: LLM docstring (vllm/entrypoints/llm.py L95-L96): 'Currently, we support "awq", "gptq", and "fp8" (experimental)'; Unsloth: 'Use fp8 for float8 KV cache to reduce memory usage by 50%.' ('이 버전' names no version.)

examples.claim: Quickstart ROCm uv install supports Python 3.12, ROCm 7.0, glibc >= 2.35; GPU page needs ROCm 6.3+, MI350 ROCm 7.0+
examples.source: quickstart.md ROCm note; gpu.rocm.inc.md requirements 'ROCm 6.3 or above - MI350 requires ROCm 7.0 or above'.

examples.claim: '--cap-add SYS_NICE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined' enables NUMA optimization with least privilege
examples.source: CPU docs: 'Instead of --privileged=true, use --cap-add SYS_NICE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined for better security.' Better than privileged, not least privilege (seccomp=unconfined drops the whole syscall filter).
